hints.title: Preserving Ties on Latest Dates
hints.text: Multiple orders can occur on the same latest date for a single product. Rank must preserve all tied orders.

hints.title: Partitioning by Product ID
hints.text: use rank() over (partition by product_id order by order_date desc) to assign rank 1 to all orders on the maximum date.

hints.title: Joining Products and Ordering Output
hints.text: join with Products to include product_name. filter for rank = 1 and order by product_name, product_id, and order_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RankedOrders AS (
    SELECT p.product_name,
           p.product_id,
           o.order_id,
           o.order_date,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY o.product_id ORDER BY o.order_date DESC) AS rnk
    FROM Orders o
    JOIN Products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id
)
SELECT product_name, product_id, order_id, order_date
FROM RankedOrders
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY product_name ASC, product_id ASC, order_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Computes ranks across partitions of products and filters top tier entries with tie handling.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Row number breaks ties arbitrarily, returning only one order rather than all orders from the latest date.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Rank window function handles simultaneous orders on the same day without subqueries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of rank() over row_number() to retain all tied entries on the most recent date.
